answer_1.quote: We use generative language models, specifically T5 encoder-decoder and GPT-2 decoder-only models ... We train reaction inference models to predict MRF dimensions from headlines.
answer_1.outputs: Free-text writer intent, reader perception, and reader action implications; categorical veracity (real/misinfo) and likelihood of spread labels.

answer_2.quote: These metrics include the BLEU (-4) ngram overlap metric and BERTScore (Zhang et al., 2020), a model-based metric for measuring semantic similarity between generated inferences and references.

answer_4.quote: For human evaluation, we assess generated inferences using the same pool of qualified workers who annotated the original data... We ask the annotators to assess the overall quality of generated implications on a 1-5 Likert scale... We also use A/B testing, showing annotators the headline with the generated implication hidden, then revealing it and asking them to re‑rate trustworthiness.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators rate overall quality (coherence, relevance) on a 1‑5 Likert scale, rate trustworthiness before and after seeing the implication, and indicate social acceptability / majority vs. minority viewpoint.
